$description: CORE / GLOBAL typography primitives. Outfit (geometric sans) is the Nockerl UI face on every platform (self-hosted on web, bundled on Android); Space Mono is the monospace. Thin-forward system: headlines run thin (100-200), body 300, 500 is the bold cap (never heavier). Sizes/line-heights are the canonical ramp; on Android 1sp maps 1:1 to these px at default density.

sans.$description: Primary UI typeface, everywhere. Outfit (geometric sans). Headlines run thin (100-200); body 300; max weight 500 (we never go heavier).

mono.$description: Monospace: ticket numbers, code, technical metadata.

thin.$description: Display + the THIN pole of emphasis-by-contrast.

light.$description: Body, chat, labels, buttons (the everyday weight).

regular.$description: Lockup product word; slightly stronger body where needed.

medium.$description: Our BOLD cap + the bold pole of emphasis. Nockerl never exceeds 500.

semibold.$description: Capped at 500, never heavier (legacy alias -> medium).

bold.$description: Capped at 500: emphasis is by CONTRAST, never additive heaviness (legacy alias -> medium).

tracking.$description: Letter-spacing scale (em). The system NEVER spreads. Uppercase is TIGHTENED, never tracked out (positive tracking reads gappy and off-brand). Three steps only: tight, snug, normal.

tight.$description: Uppercase buttons, the brand lockup, and larger uppercase labels / badges / breadcrumbs. The tightened-caps look.

eyebrow.$description: Small uppercase overline / eyebrow labels (10px caps). The tiniest caps want a touch more air than buttons. 0 = the caps ceiling; tunable on its own without touching body.

snug.$description: Large lowercase display + headings: a whisper of optical tightening so big type does not feel loose.

normal.$description: Body, prose, mono, and the loosest any uppercase ever goes. The default, usually no declaration at all.
